result.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent the diff changes the fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (undefined), which can never match, so `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` become undefined — whereas the old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. This is a real regression for updates/deletes without a stored externalCalendarId.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (the else-branch), the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined`), which will not match any real calendar externalId, yielding `undefined`. The same pattern is used in `deleteEvent` (`calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`). This is verifiably incorrect logic in the diff (it can’t select a destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided), and can lead to update/delete targeting an undefined calendar id (or falling back unintentionally if later code defaults), breaking expected behavior for events without a stored `externalCalendarId`.
